  2. Check for Lottie — Scan the selection and list nodes that may cause issues in Lottie export.


Convert to

  1. Convert to Draft — Detach, remove layout, and flatten hierarchy for a simpler draft version.
  2. Convert to Wireframe — Turn fills into black outlines for wireframe-style feedback.
  3. Convert to Blueprint — Convert the design into a blueprint-style look.


Shadows

  1. Convert Inner Shadows — Turn inner shadows into strokes so they work better in Lottie and other exports.
  2. Force Split Shadows — Split combined shadow effects into separate layers.
  3. Remove Shadow Spreads — Remove spread from drop shadows where needed.


Strokes

  1. Flatten All Strokes — Flatten strokes into fills.
  2. Outline Strokes with Caps — Outline strokes while keeping caps (round, square, etc.).
  3. Clean Up Strokes — Simplify and clean stroke setup.


When to use it

Use it when you need to prep a frame for Lottie, simplify a component for dev handoff, strip a design down to a wireframe or blueprint, or clean up a messy file before export.

model.name: Locals Only!
model.description:
Locals Only! re-binds all applied styles and variables on your selection to the current file’s local styles and variables. It can even update variables applied to component properties.


Why Locals Only!?

Resolves every applied style, variable and/or component by looking for a matching name in the current file.

  1. Preview local variable behavior of published designs from within a branch.
  2. Move components between templates and product files, and easily sync them to the product file.


How to use

  1. Select one or more layers.
  2. Decide whether or not you want to localize components.
  3. Click Analyze to generate the scope of the updates.
  4. Click Go Local to reapply local styles, variables and components to your selection.


Swapping Components (NEW)

Use the toggle next to the component section to include or exclude localizing matching components.


Components OFF applies local styles and variables to the full tree: the selection and every descendant, including inside instances.

  1. Use this when you only want to preview local styles and variables while keeping instance links as they are.
  2. Useful for branch previews.


Components ON swaps each instance to a matching local component by name (when one exists). Nested instances inside swapped components are swapped too, so everything ends up pointing at the current file.

  1. Use this when you want instances to become local components and still get local styles and variables. It will additional apply matching local styles and variables if they exist outside of components.
  2. Useful for component migration.


Details and limitations

  1. Matching is by style or variable name only (for variables, the collection name must also match).
  2. The plugin does not create styles or variables; it only rebinds to existing local ones with the same name.
  3. Large selections can take some time; consider batching to avoid freezing the tab.

Duplicate styles group

Duplicate a styles group, with optionally rebinding its variable bindings to another collection.


Duplicate variable collection

Duplicates a variable collection with its metadata and values.

Rename variables

Batch-renames variables using find/replace rules, similar to Figma’s batch rename.

Replace style variable bindings

Batch find and replaces variable bindings inside style definitions.


Replace styles

Batch finds and rebinds node style assignments to different styles based on name matching and the local style inventory. Style replacement is less smooth than with variables due to limited Figma styles API support, so it requires a two-step approach.


Replace variables

Select by styles or variables

Selects all nodes that use a specific style or variable.

Typography

model.name: File Health
model.description:
Find what's making your file heavy and fix it in place.


Big Figma files get slow, and File Health shows you why.


Most of the time it is stuff nobody can see any more. Layers someone hid and forgot. Copies of a component switched off but never deleted. A whole page pasted into a frame too small to show it, sitting just past the edge, invisible. None of it shows up on your canvas. All of it still weighs something.


File Health finds it and offers to delete it. Clear the page in one click, or go frame by frame and look first. It will not touch anything inside a component, anything hidden in one theme but shown in another, or a mask. Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes all of it.


Break down what else is making the file heavy: oversized images, deep nesting, heavy effects, massive variant sets. Offenders are ranked by severity so you know where to start. Images that are far bigger than the size you show them at can be resized in place.


Surface every outside reference in your file, the remote components, styles, and variables pulled from other libraries, so you can localize, detach, or flatten them right from the plugin.


Built for teams working in the browser across lots of shared files. No network access, no data leaves your machine.


=== === ===


The detail, for people who want it

Cleanup finds three things and offers to delete them, all at once or one frame at a time:


  1. Hidden layers, grouped by the frame they sit in.
  2. Hidden component instances. Ten instances of a row component with three hidden are three dead copies. The source component is never touched.
  3. Content clipped entirely out of view. Paste a 3000px page into an 1100px frame and roughly 2000px of it paints nothing while still costing layers. This is found by geometry, not guesswork: a layer is only offered when its bounds, padded by the reach of its own shadows and strokes, have zero overlap with the area its frame actually shows.


Never deleted: anything inside a component or an instance; a mask; a layer whose visibility is bound to a variable; a visible empty frame (those are routinely spacers and drop targets). Every layer is re-checked against the live file immediately before it is removed, because the file is multiplayer and a scan can be minutes old.


Weight ranks what is heavy across six causes: large images, dense pages, bloated containers, large variant sets, effect-heavy layers, and complex vectors. Switch between Tiers (against known-pain thresholds) and Outliers (how extreme each item is versus this file's median). Click any row to select and zoom to it. It also offers to resize an oversized image to the size it is actually displayed at, and reports the real before-and-after file size.


Outside Sources finds every component, style, and variable that lives in another file, plus broken links and heavy overrides. Fixes: Localize, Detach, Flatten.


What this plugin will not tell you

Figma does not publish how it calculates the memory meter in View > Memory usage, and states that image decoding is not counted in it at all. So File Health does not print a RAM figure: it would be a guess dressed up as a measurement. It reports what it can actually measure (layers, nodes, image pixels and dimensions) and leads with the drivers Figma itself names: hidden layers, node count, components and variants, and complex vectors.


It also cannot tell you why a component link is broken. A main component that was deleted, and one that lives in a file you cannot open, are indistinguishable through the plugin API, so the plugin says so rather than guessing.


No network access. Nothing leaves your file. Free forever.

model.name: Undetach — Tokens & Components
model.description:
Undetach keeps your design system honest, from inside the file — and now it remembers what that system used to look like.


TOKENS

Load your file's variables as an expected set, or define your own typed tokens (color, number, string, boolean). Check drift at a glance — match, drifted, or missing — and push corrections back as real Figma variables with one confirm-gated click.


COMPONENTS

Scan every component with live thumbnails, instance counts as usage bars, and deltas since your last scan. Spot a component trending toward zero before the detach wave hits your library. Find detached-instance candidates and reattach them in one click. Click any row to jump straight to it on canvas.


AUDIT

Find every fill, stroke, corner radius, auto-layout gap, padding, and font size that isn't bound to a variable, each matched to its nearest token. Values that already equal a token simply get bound (no visual change); off-token values snap to the nearest one — and never to a far one, so anything without a close match is left alone. Review findings one by one with the canvas following you (arrow keys to step, Enter to fix), or fix a whole page in one pass. Ignore the exceptions you meant to keep, and they stop coming back.


HISTORY & CHANGELOG

Every push records a named snapshot of your tokens — label, note, timestamp — stored in the file itself, so your teammates see the same history. Compare today's variables against any past snapshot ("this token was

#1D9E75 in v2"), then generate markdown release notes between any two points: tokens changed, added, and removed; components added, removed, and renamed; the biggest usage shifts. One click to copy, ready for your library publish notes, a PR, or Slack.


WHY IT'S DIFFERENT

Figma doesn't record that a frame "used to be an instance," so detach counts from scans are an honest heuristic and labelled as one — a signal to go look, not a verdict. Undetach never guesses at a token that isn't close, never writes without asking, and never sends your file anywhere.


PRIVATE BY DESIGN

No network access, enforced in the manifest. No AI. No data collection. Scans, preferences, and token history stay in your file and in Figma's local plugin storage.


Every write is confirm-gated and undoable as a single step.


Beta by Shanthan Nihal Boppani. Personal and evaluation use is free; corporate, commercial, or production use requires informing the author first — shanthan.nihal@live.com.

model.name: SVG Chart

Paste the table you already have and pick a chart type. What lands on the canvas is made of ordinary Figma shapes and text layers — no components, no variables, nothing to detach or undo afterwards.


Six types: bars, horizontal bars, line, pie, donut, radar.


It reads a table however it happened to copy. Tabs, semicolons, commas, plain spaces, markdown pipes. Quoted CSV keeps a label like “North, America” in one piece. Asana and Notion flatten a table into a single column, one cell per line, and those get put back together. Numbers survive 1 234, 1,234, 1.234,56, $739, 85.6%, +11.9 pp, the accounting (1 240) for negatives, and the minus sign that is not a hyphen. Whichever separators your source used come back on the chart, and a switch overrides that when you want something else.


Layers arrive sorted instead of as one flat pile. Grid, Scale, Axis, Bars, Values, Categories — each is its own named group. With several series, bars and lines nest one group per column, so recolouring a whole series means selecting one thing.


Columns and rows can be switched off without editing the data. Values, grid, legend, line dots and rounded shapes are switches too.


The plugin has no network access. Your table is parsed and drawn on your own machine, and nothing is sent anywhere.

model.name: Font Swap & Merge – Replace fonts, merge duplicate sizes, tidy typography
model.description:
Clean up typography across whole frames, directly on the layers. No text styles or variables needed.


Select one or more frames and Font Swap & Merge lists every font and every size inside them, with a layer count on each.


SWAP FONTS

- Pick the sizes of a font you want to change, for example Poppins 24, 20 and 18, and choose a new font.

- Weights are matched for you, so SemiBold stays SemiBold. You can change any row.

- Set up several fonts at once and apply them together.


MERGE SIZES

- See every size in use on a size spread chart.

- Get suggestions to merge near-duplicate sizes, like 15, 16 and 17 into 16.

- Round decimal sizes such as 13.5.

- Choose how close sizes must be (±0.5 to ±4 px) and whether to merge across all fonts or within one font.

- Add your own custom merges.

- Pixel line heights scale with the new size, or stay as they are.


MERGE FONTS

- Tick the fonts you want to get rid of and merge them into the one you keep. Weights are matched for each font and every size stays the same.


SAFE BY DESIGN

- Every swap or merge is a single undo step.

- Mixed text is handled run by run, so only the matching parts of a layer change.

- Layers with text styles or variables are flagged. Detach them, or skip them.

- Layers with missing fonts are skipped and easy to find. Hidden layers are skipped unless you include them.

- Select layers shows exactly what will change before you apply.

- Every section has an ⓘ tooltip that explains how it works.


HOW TO USE

1. Select frames, groups, sections or text layers.

2. Run Font Swap & Merge.

3. Swap tab: pick size chips, choose a font under Change to, then click Apply.

4. Merge tab: choose Sizes or Fonts, review the suggestions, then click Merge.

5. Changed your mind? Press ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z once.
